newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia November trade gap revised upward.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia November trade gap revised upward.

text.p: Malaysia's trade deficit in November was revised upwards to 526.4 million ringgit from a previously reported gap of 523.1 million earlier, the national Bernama news agency said on Monday.
Citing a report from the Statistics Department, Bernama said November's deficit narrowed from a deficit of 782.7 million in October.
The deficit for the month was higher than the shortfall of 39.38 million ringgit recorded in November 1995.
The deficit for the first 11 months of 1996 dropped to 1.5 billion ringgit, down a sharp 85.1 percent from a deficit of 10 billion ringgit recorded in the same period of 1995, the department added.

The drop in the cumulative deficit was the result of higher growth in exports by 7.2 percent to 179.6 billion ringgit for the 11 months from 167.5 billion ringgit for the same period of 1995, compared with a growth of only 2.0 percent in imports from 177.5 billion ringgit to 181.1 billion ringgit.
For November alone, exports totalled 16.5 billion ringgit, down from 17.0 billion ringgit in the same month of 1995, while imports also declined to 17.0 billion from 17.1 billion ringgit previously.
